transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Celerity Head of ML), Priya Patel (Infra), Jorge Alvarez (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated; some on-prem experiments with vLLM/TGI; questions about API compatibility, eval parity and security.

00:00 Liam: Hey all, yeah thanks for doing this. We wanted to get a sense of Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted and whether we can migrate our PROD traffic off OpenAI with minimal changes.
00:07 Maya: Absolutely, thanks for the time. Quick intro - I'm Maya, AE, and Carlos is our SE who will take the deep dive.
00:12 Carlos: Hey everybody. I'll be curious about your current invocation patterns and what latency SLA you expect.
00:18 Liam: Sure. Right now we're on OpenAI for most user-facing generation. Latency needs to be under 800ms p50 for short prompts, and p95 ideally under 1.5s. Cost is creeping up - we're seeing token spend jump with 3x growth.
00:30 Priya: We also run some on-prem experiments where we spin up vLLM stacks and a T G I front-end for special customers, but that's not production yet; it's brittle for autoscaling.
00:42 Carlos: Makes sense. Are you using any custom KV cache / prefix caching today?
00:46 Liam: We do some caching in our app layer for repeated prompts, but not model-level KV cache yet.
00:52 Maya: Okay. High level, Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, autoscale policies and can be deployed in your VPC or as a fully managed dedicated instance. Redwood Private is our private control plane / on-prem option when you need air-gap or strict data residency.
01:10 Jorge: If we move to Dedicated, how much work is it to change our client code that calls the OpenAI endpoints? We have a bunch of microservices calling the API.
01:18 Carlos: We provide OpenAI-compatible API endpoints for common call patterns (completion/chat/embeddings). Most customers get 95%+ compatibility out of the box; there are some edge cases around streaming chunking and tool-calling webhooks that we help adjust.
01:32 Priya: Important for us is eval parity. We have a 2000-prompt eval suite; if we migrate, we need identical outputs or at least deterministic deltas. How do we validate that?
01:44 Carlos: Great question. We run model parity tests — you feed us your evals and we run them across the target model variants and quantify diff rates. Also important: model variants and quantization can introduce small differences. We can pin model versions to minimize drift.
01:58 Liam: What about the stack underneath? We're seeing people mention vLLM and TGI — if we bring your Dedicated in our infra, will you support those runtimes or is it your own serving runtime?
02:11 Maya: Redwood's serving runtime is our GPU-optimized engine; we support multiple runners under the hood and have integrations for TGI and vLLM in some cases, but Dedicated customers get our managed runtime tuned for batching, KV cache, and quantized kernels. That usually yields better throughput/latency than vanilla vLLM in our experience.
02:30 Priya: Any gotchas around model artifacts? We host some finetuned models and private weights on S3.
02:36 Carlos: You can bring your weights. For Dedicated we support customer-provided model artifacts stored in your VPC/S3 buckets. We integrate with KMS/HSM for encryption at rest and during deployment.
02:47 Jorge: Are there SOC2 / audit logs and role-based access?
02:51 Maya: Yes — Dedicated includes audit logs, RBAC, SSO (SAML/OIDC) integrations. For Private we can offer additional compliance packages and longer log retention.
03:00 Liam: Good. On pricing: at volume, does Dedicated become cheaper than OpenAI?
03:06 Maya: Typically yes for heavy throughput. Dedicated is reserved capacity so unit cost per token drops, but there's a commit and minimum. We'll send a sizing/pricing deck.
03:15 Priya: For autoscaling, we care about burst handling. We have traffic spikes 2-3x during certain jobs. How fast can Dedicated scale?
03:24 Carlos: There are options — predictable autoscale policies and burst pools. Scaling is bounded by cold-starts for GPUs; we recommend a small buffer of warm instances or burst capacity. We can show historical scaling graphs in the Console.
03:36 Liam: Benchmarking — we'd like Redwood to run our evals and simulate traffic. What's involved?
03:40 Carlos: Usually two phases: functional parity (your eval set) then perf run under simulated traffic patterns. We capture token-level latency, cost, and KV cache hit rates. We'll need your eval set and some representative concurrency numbers.
03:53 Liam: We'll share that. One thing: we're using tool-calling heavily, and our app relies on predictably-ordered streaming tokens, sometimes with mid-stream cancel. Does Redwood stream support that?
04:05 Carlos: Streaming is supported; tool-calling and function-calls are supported but sometimes customers need to tweak chunk sizes or adjust their client. We can help with client libraries.
04:17 Jorge: Any limits on request size or context length compared to OpenAI?
04:21 Carlos: We support large contexts; limits depend on model and deployment. We can provision models with larger context windows if needed, though cost and memory footprint increase.
04:31 Priya: Network and Egress — if Dedicated is in our VPC, is egress charged? How does data flow?
04:36 Maya: If Dedicated is deployed into your cloud account / VPC, egress is your cloud's normal cost. For fully managed Redwood-hosted we absorb egress but that's priced into the plan. We'll provide architecture notes depending on which mode you pick.
04:50 Liam: What about rollout strategy? We want canary and gradual cutover.
04:54 Carlos: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. You can route a percentage of traffic to Dedicated and fall back to Hosted/OpenAI on failures.
05:04 Jorge: Great. One operational question: how do we do model upgrades and versioning?
05:08 Carlos: Versioning is per-model and per-route. You can pin routes to model versions and do A/B or canary. We also expose per-route telemetry in the Console.
05:16 Liam: Any previous customers who migrated from OpenAI you can share a short example of latency improvements?
05:20 Maya: Yes — we've migrated a few mid-market customers who saw 20-40% lower p95 after tuning batching and enabling KV cache. We'll anonymize exact numbers in the doc.
05:31 Priya: Security deep dive will be required for us. We have an internal security review board. Do you have SOC2 attestations and a security pack?
05:40 Maya: We do. We'll attach SOC2, data processing agreements, and our security package. For Private and some Enterprise Dedicated deals we can support additional assessments.
05:50 Liam: On data retention: we need logs for 1 year for debugging but want content redaction in some cases.
05:57 Carlos: Audit logs are configurable; content retention policies can be set and we support PII redaction hooks.
06:05 Jorge: For the eval parity — if we see output deltas after migration, do you assist with retuning/prompts or would that be on us?
06:12 Carlos: We offer primer work where our SEs help with prompt engineering and quantization guidance to minimize regression. That is typically scoped as part of a pilot.
06:20 Liam: Can Dedicated run in our AWS account?
06:23 Maya: Yes, Dedicated can be deployed into your cloud account or in Redwood-managed infra with network peering.
06:29 Priya: What about hardware—GPUs types supported? We have preferences for A100s for certain models.
06:34 Carlos: We support A10/A100/H100 depending on region and plan. Sizing depends on model size and throughput needs.
06:41 Jorge: Another question — do you handle secrets for model access? We would enforce KMS usage.
06:46 Maya: We integrate with customer KMS and support HSM where required. Secrets are never stored in plaintext in the control plane.
06:53 Liam: Ok sounds good. I'd like to propose a benchmark: run 3 models (gpt-3.5-style open model, a 13B finetuned variant, and our smaller 7B finetuned) against our eval set at 50 RPS for 10 minutes each, capture p50/p95/p99, token cost and drift. Will Redwood run that?
07:10 Carlos: Yes, we can run that as part of a pilot. We'll document the test harness and run it on Dedicated infra.
07:18 Priya: We also need to validate streaming order determinism for our tool-calls.
07:22 Carlos: Make a note, we'll include a streaming determinism test.
07:25 Maya: So immediate next steps: we'll send the pricing and sizing doc, security pack and benchmark checklist. Let's target the pilot next week if we can get the evals.
07:34 Liam: Sounds good. If we like the results, timeline for production migration? We want a 6-8 week window after pilot.
07:39 Maya: That's reasonable. Pilot -> small canary -> ramp. We'll partner on the rollout plan.
07:45 Jorge: Any constraints around our CI/CD? We use Terraform for infra and GitHub Actions for deployment.
07:50 Carlos: We provide Terraform modules and deployment guides; GitHub Actions friendly.
07:55 Priya: One more nit: are there SDKs we can drop in or do we need to rewire a lot?
07:59 Carlos: We have OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs for Python/TS that make the swap minimal. Some customers do a find-replace on endpoints and a couple of small changes for streaming.
08:08 Liam: Okay excellent. Anything else we should flag?
08:10 Maya: Just privacy/regulatory - if you have EU residency requirements we can place Dedicated in the EU region and provide data residency guarantees in the contract.
08:20 Liam: Good.

(Brief pause while people check notes)

25:00 Maya: Sorry for the gap, we had a scheduling overlap. Back to action items recap.
25:06 Maya: Action items: Maya to send pricing, Carlos to send perf checklist, Liam to share evals. We'll schedule the infra deep-dive with Priya.
25:18 Priya: I'll invite two infra SREs to that deep-dive.
25:22 Jorge: We'll also attach our tokenization notes and prompt libs.
25:27 Carlos: Also, if you have any finetuned artifacts we should test, share the model weights location and access method.
25:34 Liam: We'll provide S3 URIs and temporary credentials.

40:12 Maya: Quick note — on rollback, you'll be able to route back to OpenAI automatically if errors exceed threshold. We can set the circuit-breaker.
40:21 Priya: Perfect.
40:25 Liam: Great call. We'll expect your emails and then book the deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
40:30 Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

(End of transcript)

Notes: transcription contains some auto-caption errors (e.g., T G I spelled out, KV as K V). References to pricing and exact hardware will be in the follow-up deck.
